items.title: 9.2 Lewis concept of acids and bases

source_refs.note: Topic 9.2, printed page 191, with Quick Check 9.1 (page 192).

blocks.text: In 1923, G.N. Lewis proposed a generalized definition of acid-base behavior in which acids and bases are identified by their ability to accept or to donate a pair of electrons and form a coordinate covalent bond.

blocks.title: Lewis acid and Lewis base
blocks.text: A Lewis acid is any species (molecule or ion) that can accept a pair of electrons, and a Lewis base is any species (molecule or ion) that can donate a pair of electrons.
A Lewis acid-base reaction occurs when a base donates a pair of electrons to an acid.

In the following reaction, each of two ammonia molecules, Lewis bases, donates a pair of electrons to a positively charged silver ion, the Lewis acid. The sum of charges on the left side is +1, so the acid-base adduct on the right hand side must carry a charge of +1:

blocks.alt: 2 H-N(H)-H with a red lone pair on N, labelled Lewis base, plus Ag+, labelled Lewis acid, arrow to the bracketed ion [H3N→Ag←NH3]+ in which each N gives its pair to Ag through a coordinate arrow, labelled Acid base adduct.
blocks.caption: Reaction of ammonia (Lewis base) with silver ion (Lewis acid) (original drawing after the scheme printed on p191 of the textbook).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The label under the adduct is printed “Alcid base adduct”; it is acid-base adduct.

The boron atom in boron trifluoride, BF₃, has only six electrons in its valence shell. Since the boron atom has an incomplete octet, it can behave as an electron pair acceptor. As a result, BF₃ is a very good Lewis acid and reacts with many Lewis bases; a fluoride ion is the Lewis base in this reaction, donating one of its lone pairs:

blocks.alt: A fluoride ion with four lone pairs and a minus charge, labelled Lewis base, plus BF3 drawn with B bonded to three F atoms each carrying three lone pairs, labelled Lewis acid, arrow to the bracketed ion [BF4]- in which one F gives a pair to B through a coordinate arrow (F→B), labelled Acid base adduct.
blocks.caption: Reaction of fluoride ion (Lewis base) with boron trifluoride (Lewis acid) (original drawing after the scheme printed on p191 of the textbook).

blocks.text: The negative charge on the adduct is the sum of charges on the left hand side of the equation is -1, the sum of charges on the right hand side must also be -1.
